NO "EVERYTHING" TOPIC
============================================================

Do not create:

    *

or:

    everything

as an unlimited public subscription by default.

A wildcard subscription can create:

    huge bandwidth
    resource exhaustion
    unclear contracts

If wildcard subscriptions already exist internally, do not expose
them publicly unless explicitly justified and bounded.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION REQUEST
============================================================

Define an explicit immutable request model.

Conceptually:

    {
        "type": "subscribe",
        "channel": "telemetry",
        "session_id": "...",
        "driver_id": "...",
        "vehicle_id": "...",
        "from": "...",
        "to": "...",
        "options": {...}
    }

Adapt exactly to repository conventions.

Do not accept arbitrary filter expressions.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION VALIDATION
============================================================

Validate:

    channel
    session
    driver
    vehicle
    timestamp range
    options
    page/window bounds
    mode

Reject invalid subscription requests with the public error model.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION RESPONSE
============================================================

Return explicit acknowledgement.

Conceptually:

    {
        "type": "subscribed",
        "subscription_id": "...",
        "channel": "...",
        "session_id": "...",
        "api_version": "v1"
    }

Use repository conventions.

============================================================
UNSUBSCRIBE
============================================================

Support explicit unsubscribe.

Conceptually:

    {
        "type": "unsubscribe",
        "subscription_id": "..."
    }

A removed subscription must stop receiving data.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION ID
============================================================

Use an explicit subscription ID.

Prefer deterministic or scoped identity where practical.

Do not expose internal object addresses.

Do not rely on random identity for correctness.

============================================================
MULTIPLE SUBSCRIPTIONS
============================================================

A single client may have multiple subscriptions where supported.

Each subscription must be independently tracked.

Do not allow one subscription to corrupt another.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION ISOLATION
============================================================

A subscription for:

    Session A

must not receive:

    Session B

data.

A subscription for:

    Driver A

must not receive:

    Driver B

data unless explicitly requested.

============================================================
SESSION BINDING
============================================================

If a subscription is session-scoped:

    bind it to an explicit session.

Do not silently switch a subscription to another session.

============================================================
MODE
============================================================

Support established:

    LIVE
    REPLAY

semantics.

Do not infer mode from:

    connection time
    wall clock

Use explicit request/state where the underlying runtime supports it.

============================================================
REPLAY SUBSCRIPTIONS
============================================================

Public WebSocket replay streams must respect:

    replay timeline
    replay session
    replay generation
    seeking
    pause
    resume
    speed

where supported.

Do not implement a second replay controller.

============================================================
REPLAY SEEK
============================================================

If existing replay architecture emits a generation/seek transition,
forward it through the public subscription contract.

Clients must be able to identify that:

    prior future data may no longer be valid.

Potential control message:

    replay.seek
    replay.generation

Use existing protocol conventions where available.

============================================================
NO FUTURE-DATA LEAK
============================================================

A replay subscription must not accidentally send future replay data
because it was already buffered before a backwards seek.

Any buffered public messages invalidated by a replay seek/generation
change must be discarded or invalidated according to existing
transport semantics.

============================================================
LIVE TELEMETRY
============================================================

Telemetry subscriptions should use existing canonical telemetry.

Do not generate telemetry in the WebSocket layer.

============================================================
TELEMETRY AUTHORITY
============================================================

Public telemetry messages must preserve the distinction between:

    observed/canonical telemetry

and:

    predicted telemetry

Never merge them into one ambiguous message type.

============================================================
PREDICTION CHANNEL
============================================================

If predictions are exposed:

    clearly mark:

        predicted
        source timestamp
        target timestamp
        horizon
        provenance

Do not allow predicted positions to masquerade as observed positions.

============================================================
ANALYTICS CHANNEL
============================================================

Analytics are derived.

Expose explicit:

    analytics

classification.

============================================================
BATTLE CHANNEL
============================================================

If battle intelligence is exposed:

    identify it as derived.

Do not make battle state canonical.

============================================================
STRATEGY CHANNEL
============================================================

If strategy is exposed:

    identify derived/observed semantics.

Do not expose strategy commands.

============================================================
INCIDENT CHANNEL
============================================================

If incident intelligence is exposed:

    preserve:

        observed
        derived
        suspected
        confirmed

semantics.

Do not strengthen uncertainty.

============================================================
COMMENTARY CHANNEL
============================================================

If commentary events/output are exposed:

    preserve:

        OBSERVED
        DERIVED
        PREDICTIVE

where upstream supports it.

AI-generated commentary must not become race authority.

============================================================
TTS OVER WEBSOCKET
============================================================

Do NOT stream raw TTS audio through Agent 17.4 unless existing
Phase 11/13 architecture already provides a specific binary audio
transport.

Public TTS transport is a future integration concern.

============================================================
MESSAGE TYPES
============================================================

Define a compact public message envelope.

Possible:

    event
    snapshot
    error
    subscribed
    unsubscribed
    heartbeat
    replay_state
    stream_started
    stream_ended

Use only required types.

============================================================
MESSAGE ENVELOPE
============================================================

A message may contain:

    api_version
    schema_version
    message_type
    message_id
    sequence
    session_id
    mode
    timestamp
    payload
    provenance

Only include fields that have a real purpose.

============================================================
MESSAGE ID
============================================================

Use explicit message identity where needed.

Do not expose internal memory addresses.

============================================================
SEQUENCE NUMBERS
============================================================

Real-time clients need ordering.

Use existing upstream sequence numbers where available.

If public sequence is required:

    define a per-subscription or per-stream monotonic sequence.

Do not use wall-clock timestamps as sequence numbers.

============================================================
SEQUENCE SEMANTICS
============================================================

Document:

    monotonicity
    reset conditions
    reconnect behaviour
    replay seek behaviour
    session change behaviour

============================================================
NO GLOBAL SEQUENCE ASSUMPTION
============================================================

Do not assume one global sequence across:

    telemetry
    events
    analytics
    predictions

unless the existing protocol explicitly defines such a sequence.

============================================================
MESSAGE ORDERING
============================================================

Preserve source ordering.

If multiple source messages share timestamps:

    use source sequence.

Do not rely on dictionary order.

============================================================
BACKPRESSURE
============================================================

Reuse existing Phase 11 outbound backpressure/rate control.

Do NOT create a second public-only backpressure engine if one exists.

The WebSocket must remain safe under slow consumers.

============================================================
SLOW CLIENT POLICY
============================================================

Define behaviour for clients that cannot consume messages quickly.

Potential:

    bounded queue
    drop oldest
    drop newest
    disconnect slow client

Use repository/Phase 11 conventions.

Do NOT silently allow unlimited queue growth.

============================================================
DROP POLICY
============================================================

If messages can be dropped, document whether:

    telemetry samples may be dropped
    state snapshots may be coalesced
    critical events may not be dropped

Do not apply a universal drop policy blindly.

============================================================
CRITICAL EVENT DELIVERY
============================================================

If existing transport architecture marks critical events:

    preserve that priority.

Examples:

    race control
    retirement
    major incident

Do not create a completely new priority system.

============================================================
TELEMETRY COALESCING
============================================================

Do not coalesce canonical event messages in ways that change meaning.

For high-frequency telemetry:

    use existing transport sampling/coalescing if available.

Do not implement uncontrolled sampling here.

============================================================
HEARTBEAT
============================================================

Use existing Phase 11 heartbeat/ping/pong infrastructure.

Do NOT create a second heartbeat protocol if one already exists.

============================================================
PING/PONG
============================================================

Follow WebSocket framework/native behaviour where possible.

Do not send application-level pings unnecessarily.

============================================================
CONNECTION TIMEOUT
============================================================

Use existing transport timeout semantics.

Do not create arbitrary timeouts without configuration.

============================================================
DISCONNECT
============================================================

Handle:

    client disconnect
    server shutdown
    upstream failure
    authentication failure later
    authorization failure later
    subscription failure

Clean all bounded connection/subscription state.

============================================================
RECONNECT
============================================================

Do NOT build a client SDK here.

Define server-side semantics for reconnect.

Clients should be able to reconnect and resubscribe.

If resume tokens/sequence replay already exist internally:

    adapt them where safe.

Do not implement a full replay-from-offset system unless existing
architecture already supports it.

============================================================
DUPLICATE DELIVERY
============================================================

Where possible, prevent duplicate public messages caused by:

    duplicate subscription
    duplicate event forwarding
    reconnect bugs

Do not create unbounded duplicate history.

============================================================
AUTHENTICATION BOUNDARY
============================================================

Agent 17.5 owns authentication.

Agent 17.4 must provide a clear pre-authentication/authorization
hook.

Possible conceptual flow:

    CONNECT
      ↓
    Version validation
      ↓
    Authentication hook
      ↓
    Authorization hook
      ↓
    Subscription
      ↓
    Delivery

Do not implement token validation in 17.4 unless an existing
authentication mechanism already exists.

============================================================
AUTHORIZATION BOUNDARY
============================================================

Support future authorization decisions per:

    channel
    session
    resource
    action

Do not hard-code privileged access into routing logic.

============================================================
ANONYMOUS ACCESS
============================================================

If public read-only channels are allowed before 17.5:

    explicitly classify them.

Do not accidentally expose privileged channels.

============================================================
RATE LIMITING BOUNDARY
============================================================

Agent 17.6 owns API rate limiting.

17.4 MUST NOT implement a second rate limiter.

However, the architecture must expose enough information for
17.6 to limit:

    connections
    subscriptions
    messages
    control requests
    channel volume

============================================================
CONTROL MESSAGE LIMITS
============================================================

Protect:

    subscribe
    unsubscribe
    replay controls where exposed

from unlimited client spam.

Do not implement the full rate limiter.

Basic validation against pathological payload size is acceptable.

============================================================
REQUEST SIZE
============================================================

Bound inbound WebSocket message size.

Reject oversized messages before parsing large payloads where the
framework allows.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION COUNT
============================================================

Set an explicit maximum subscription count per connection if
needed.

Do not permit unbounded subscriptions.

============================================================
CONNECTION COUNT
============================================================

Do not create global connection accounting if Agent 17.11 owns
monitoring, but expose a hook for future connection limits.

============================================================
PAYLOAD SIZE
============================================================

Public messages must be bounded.

High-volume telemetry must use bounded payloads.

============================================================
JSON SERIALIZATION
============================================================

Use stable JSON unless the existing protocol explicitly defines
another encoding.

============================================================
BINARY MESSAGES
============================================================

Do not introduce binary protobuf/msgpack/etc. merely for Agent 17.4.

If Phase 11 already uses an established binary format:

    reuse it where public-safe.

============================================================
SCHEMA VERSION
============================================================

Public WebSocket messages must have explicit schema/version metadata
consistent with Agent 17.2.

Do not create a second incompatible version system.

============================================================
ERROR MESSAGE
============================================================

Define a public structured WS error envelope.

Conceptually:

    {
        "type": "error",
        "error": {
            "code": "...",
            "message": "...",
            "request_id": "...",
            "details": ...
        }
    }

Do not expose stack traces.

============================================================
ERROR CODES
============================================================

Potential:

    INVALID_MESSAGE
    INVALID_SUBSCRIPTION
    UNSUPPORTED_VERSION
    UNKNOWN_CHANNEL
    SESSION_NOT_FOUND
    INVALID_CURSOR
    INVALID_RANGE
    FORBIDDEN
    AUTH_REQUIRED
    RATE_LIMITED
    SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
    INTERNAL_ERROR

Only use those actually needed.

============================================================
ERROR CONSISTENCY
============================================================

Reuse Agent 17.1 public API error semantics.

REST and WebSocket should communicate equivalent error meaning.

============================================================
NO INTERNAL EXCEPTIONS
============================================================

Never send:

    SQLAlchemy exception
    stack trace
    provider exception
    file paths
    credentials

to clients.

============================================================
PUBLIC DTO BOUNDARY
============================================================

Never serialize internal domain objects directly.

Use:

    internal object
       ↓
    public message adapter
       ↓
    JSON

============================================================
DOMAIN ISOLATION
============================================================

WebSocket handlers must not:

    modify domain models
    modify canonical telemetry
    modify analytics
    modify predictions

unless an explicitly existing service mutation is public-safe and
future authentication/authorization supports it.

Prefer read-only delivery.

============================================================
READ-ONLY DEFAULT
============================================================

Public WebSocket messages should primarily subscribe to state/events.

Do NOT expose public commands for:

    Director
    cameras
    OBS
    race control
    telemetry
    prediction
    strategy

============================================================
REPLAY COMMANDS
============================================================

If existing public architecture requires replay controls such as:

    play
    pause
    seek
    speed

do NOT implement them as unrestricted commands in Agent 17.4.

Establish only a safe adapter boundary if an existing public-safe
replay service exists.

Any control API must eventually pass authentication/authorization.

============================================================
NO TELEMETRY INJECTION
============================================================

Do NOT implement:

    publish telemetry
    inject event
    modify prediction

through WebSocket.

============================================================
NO RACE CONTROL
============================================================

Do NOT expose public commands for:

    red flag
    safety car
    session status

as mutable operations.

============================================================
NO OBS CONTROL
============================================================

Do NOT implement:

    switch scene
    set source
    camera control

============================================================
NO STREAM CONTROL
============================================================

Do NOT implement:

    start stream
    stop stream
    change platform

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION FILTERS
============================================================

Use explicit allow-listed filters.

Examples:

    session_id
    driver_id
    vehicle_id
    event_type
    start_time
    end_time

Do NOT accept arbitrary expressions.

============================================================
FILTER VALIDATION
============================================================

Validate:

    type
    range
    identifiers
    timestamps

Reject invalid values.

============================================================
TIME RANGE
============================================================

Public subscriptions to high-volume events may specify:

    start
    end

but must be bounded.

Do not allow an unlimited historical replay query through the
real-time endpoint.

============================================================
LIVE STREAM START
============================================================

For a live subscription, define whether the client receives:

    current state snapshot
    then incremental events

or:

    only future events

Choose the model based on existing Phase 11 transport behavior.

Document it.

============================================================
SNAPSHOT + DELTA MODEL
============================================================

If useful:

    subscription accepted
         ↓
    initial snapshot
         ↓
    incremental updates

This can prevent clients from requiring hidden state.

Use existing runtime snapshots.

============================================================
NO SECOND SNAPSHOT AUTHORITY
============================================================

Do not create a WebSocket-owned race snapshot.

Adapt existing state snapshots.

============================================================
TELEMETRY FREQUENCY
============================================================

Do not invent a new telemetry sampling rate.

Use existing canonical/provider transport configuration where
possible.

============================================================
ANALYTICS FREQUENCY
============================================================

Analytics subscriptions should emit on:

    actual state changes
    established analytics sequence

not every connection tick.

============================================================
COMMENTARY EVENT DELIVERY
============================================================

Commentary events should be delivered as discrete events.

Do not repeatedly send unchanged commentary state.

============================================================
PREDICTION DELIVERY
============================================================

Prediction updates should preserve:

    source timestamp
    target timestamp
    horizon
    prediction classification
    quality/provenance where available

============================================================
REPLAY GENERATION
============================================================

When replay generation changes:

    clients must be able to identify the new generation.

Do not allow sequence numbers from generation 1 to be interpreted as
generation 2 without explicit semantics.

============================================================
SESSION CHANGES
============================================================

When runtime session changes:

    subscriptions bound to the old session must be invalidated or
    explicitly transitioned according to existing architecture.

Do not silently change their session.

============================================================
SHUTDOWN
============================================================

Server shutdown must:

    stop new subscriptions
    close active connections gracefully where possible
    release bounded state
    not mutate canonical state

============================================================
RESOURCE CLEANUP
============================================================

On disconnect:

    remove subscriptions
    remove connection-local queues
    remove callbacks/listeners
    release temporary resources

No leaked subscriptions.

============================================================
LISTENER LEAK TEST
============================================================

Repeated:

    connect
    subscribe
    disconnect

must not grow internal listener counts indefinitely.

============================================================
EVENT LISTENER OWNERSHIP
============================================================

Do not register a new unbounded listener for every request without
cleanup.

Reuse existing subscription infrastructure if possible.

============================================================
CONCURRENCY
============================================================

Multiple clients may subscribe simultaneously.

Verify:

    client A receives A's subscription data
    client B receives B's subscription data

No cross-client leakage.

============================================================
CONCURRENT SUBSCRIPTIONS
============================================================

One connection with:

    telemetry + events + analytics

must not corrupt subscription state.

============================================================
BACKPRESSURE CONCURRENCY
============================================================

A slow Client A must not block:

    healthy Client B

unless existing Phase 11 architecture explicitly defines shared
backpressure.

============================================================
SECURITY
============================================================

Before Agent 17.5, public authentication must be considered a hook.

Do NOT embed:

    API keys
    passwords
    tokens

in code.

============================================================
ORIGIN / CORS
============================================================

Inspect existing deployment policy.

Do not automatically allow every origin.

If origin validation already exists:

    reuse it.

============================================================
WEBSOCKET CLOSE CODES
============================================================

Use standard WebSocket close semantics where appropriate.

Do not invent arbitrary close codes without justification.

============================================================
KEEPALIVE
============================================================

Reuse existing transport keepalive.

============================================================
NO POLLING LOOP
============================================================

Do not create:

    while True:
        sleep(...)
        poll database

to deliver real-time messages if the repository already has event/
subscription infrastructure.

============================================================
NO DATABASE POLLING
============================================================

WebSocket delivery should consume established runtime/events.

Do not query the database every few milliseconds.

============================================================
NO EXTERNAL API POLLING
============================================================

Do not call:

    FastF1
    Ergast
    API-Sports
    other F1 APIs

from the WebSocket layer.

============================================================
NO AI
============================================================

Do not add:

    LLM
    ML
    AI

to the WebSocket API.

============================================================
NO COMMENTARY GENERATION
============================================================

Do not generate commentary text.

============================================================
NO TTS
============================================================

Do not synthesize audio.

============================================================
NO DIRECTOR
============================================================

Do not control Director/cameras.

============================================================
NO OBS
============================================================

Do not control OBS.

============================================================
NO STREAMING PROVIDERS
============================================================

Do not publish directly to:

    Twitch
    YouTube
    Kick

Create a dedicated WebSocket API test suite using the repository's

Potential location:

    tests/api/
    tests/websocket/
    tests/transport/

Use the existing convention.

============================================================
DETERMINISTIC SUBSCRIBE TEST
============================================================

Connect:

    Client A

Send:

    subscribe telemetry
    session = SESSION-A
    driver = DRIVER-A

Expected:

    subscribed acknowledgement
    correct API version
    correct subscription ID

Then emit:

    Driver A telemetry.

Expected:

    Client A receives it.

Emit:

    Driver B telemetry.

Expected:

    Client A does NOT receive it.

============================================================
SESSION ISOLATION TEST
============================================================

Subscription:

    SESSION-A

Emit:

    SESSION-B event

Expected:

    no delivery to SESSION-A subscription.

============================================================
MULTI-SUBSCRIPTION TEST
============================================================

One client:

    subscription 1 = telemetry
    subscription 2 = events

Verify independent delivery.

============================================================
DUPLICATE SUBSCRIPTION TEST
============================================================

Attempt duplicate identical subscription.

Expected:

    deterministic behaviour:

        reject
        reuse
        or clearly create separate subscription

Choose and document one policy.

Do not accidentally duplicate delivery.

============================================================
UNSUBSCRIBE TEST
============================================================

Subscribe.

Receive event.

Unsubscribe.

Emit new event.

Expected:

    no further delivery.

============================================================
DISCONNECT CLEANUP TEST
============================================================

Subscribe.

Disconnect.

Emit event.

Expected:

    no delivery
    listener/queue cleaned.

============================================================
BACKPRESSURE TEST
============================================================

Create:

    slow Client A
    healthy Client B

Flood Client A.

Expected:

    bounded Client A resources.

Client B continues to receive data.

============================================================
EVENT-STORM TEST
============================================================

Generate a high volume event burst.

Expected:

    bounded memory
    deterministic queue/drop/disconnect behaviour
    no process-wide failure.

Do NOT use real sleep.

============================================================
MESSAGE SIZE TEST
============================================================

Send oversized control message.

Expected:

    safe rejection/close according to policy.

No huge allocation.

============================================================
MALFORMED MESSAGE TEST
============================================================

Send:

    invalid JSON

Expected:

    structured error / safe close.

No traceback.

============================================================
UNKNOWN CHANNEL TEST
============================================================

Send:

    subscribe unknown_channel

Expected:

    UNKNOWN_CHANNEL

============================================================
VERSION TEST
============================================================

Connect to:

    unsupported public API version.

Expected:

    explicit version error.

Do not downgrade.

============================================================
PREDICTION TEST
============================================================

Subscribe to:

    predictions

Verify message contains clear distinction:

    predicted

and not:

    observed.

============================================================
REPLAY SEEK TEST
============================================================

Subscribe to replay stream.

Process:

    generation 1
    data at T=100

Seek backwards.

Generation changes.

Expected:

    stale buffered data from generation 1 is not delivered as current
    generation 2 data.

============================================================
LIVE / REPLAY TEST
============================================================

Equivalent event streams under:

    LIVE
    REPLAY

must maintain equivalent public message semantics.

============================================================
NO-FUTURE TEST
============================================================

At replay time:

    T=100

Do not send observed event:

    T=105

before replay reaches it.

============================================================
CANONICAL MUTATION TEST
============================================================

Snapshot canonical state.

Connect and subscribe.

Send/receive messages.

Verify canonical state is unchanged.

============================================================
ANALYTICS MUTATION TEST
============================================================

Snapshot analytics.

Subscribe.

Verify unchanged.

============================================================
CONCURRENT CLIENT TEST
============================================================

Clients:

    A → Driver A
    B → Driver B

Emit:

    A event
    B event

Verify no cross-delivery.

============================================================
RECONNECT TEST
============================================================

Client connects.

Subscribes.

Disconnects.

Reconnects.

Resubscribes.

Verify:

    no duplicate stale subscriptions
    no listener leak
    correct new connection state.

============================================================
HEARTBEAT TEST
============================================================

Reuse existing heartbeat/keepalive.

Verify dead connection cleanup.

============================================================
NO-POLLING TEST
============================================================

Inspect implementation to verify WebSocket delivery does not
introduce periodic database polling.

============================================================
OPENAPI / DOCUMENTATION BOUNDARY
============================================================

WebSocket details may not be represented completely in OpenAPI.

Do not try to force the complete WS protocol into REST schemas.

Agent 17.7 owns formal API documentation.

Provide machine-readable models and clear documentation so 17.7 can
document the protocol.

AUTHENTICATION PREPARATION
============================================================

Expose a clean connection/subscription authentication hook.

Do NOT implement Agent 17.5.

Future authentication must be able to establish:

    principal
    scopes
    permissions

without rewriting the WS transport.

============================================================
RATE LIMIT PREPARATION
============================================================

Expose information required for Agent 17.6 to limit:

    connection rate
    subscription rate
    control messages
    per-client bandwidth

Do NOT implement Agent 17.6.

============================================================
MONITORING PREPARATION
============================================================

Expose enough structured metadata for Agent 17.11:

    connection ID
    API version
    channel
    subscription ID
    message type
    status

Do not implement full monitoring.

CODE QUALITY
============================================================

Follow actual project standards:

    leaky bucket

    retry-after
    429
    backpressure
    abuse
    connection limit

11. Inspect existing configuration.

12. Inspect existing cache/state abstractions.

13. Inspect tests.

14. Inspect:

    pyproject.toml
    Makefile
    .github/workflows/

Do NOT assume paths.

============================================================
REUSE EXISTING RATE-LIMITING PRIMITIVES
============================================================

If Phase 11 or another subsystem already contains:

    token bucket
    leaky bucket
    sliding window
    concurrency limiter
    backpressure limiter

reuse it where appropriate.

Do NOT create a competing rate-limit architecture.

============================================================
ONE SHARED POLICY MODEL
============================================================

REST and WebSocket rate limiting should use a common conceptual
policy model.

Do NOT create unrelated:

    RestRateLimiter
    WebSocketRateLimiter

with different policy languages.

Transport-specific adapters may exist, but policy must remain shared.

============================================================
RATE-LIMITING VS AUTHENTICATION
============================================================

Authentication answers:

    who?

Rate limiting answers:

    how much traffic is allowed?

Do not make rate limiting responsible for credential validation.

============================================================
RATE-LIMITING VS AUTHORIZATION
============================================================

Authorization answers:

    what can the client access?

Rate limiting answers:

    how often/how much can they consume?

Do not use rate limits as an authorization mechanism.

============================================================
RATE-LIMITING KEY
============================================================

The limiter must use a safe client key.

Possible dimensions:

    principal_id
    API key ID
    client/network identity
    endpoint
    API version
    subscription ID
    connection ID

Prefer the strongest available stable identity.

Do NOT key authenticated requests only by IP when principal identity
is available.

============================================================
ANONYMOUS CLIENTS
============================================================

For unauthenticated access, use the safest available client
identity.

Be cautious with shared NAT/proxy environments.

Do not create a rate-limit policy that unfairly blocks an entire
internet population solely because many users share an address,
unless that is an explicitly chosen edge-control policy.

============================================================
TRUSTED PROXY HEADERS
============================================================

Do NOT blindly trust:

    X-Forwarded-For
    X-Real-IP
    Forwarded

unless the deployment architecture explicitly marks the proxy as
trusted.

A client must not bypass rate limits merely by spoofing a header.

============================================================
CLIENT IDENTITY NORMALIZATION
============================================================

Normalize client identity before rate-limit key creation.

Do not create multiple keys for the same logical authenticated
principal merely because transport metadata differs.

============================================================
POLICY SCOPE
============================================================

Support rate limits at useful levels.

Possible scopes:

    global
    principal
    API key
    endpoint
    route
    API version
    WebSocket connection
    subscription
    control message

Do NOT implement all possible combinations unless justified.

Start with a minimal coherent policy hierarchy.

============================================================
GLOBAL LIMIT
============================================================

A global limit MAY protect the entire public API process.

Use carefully.

A global limit must not accidentally make one abusive client able
to starve all other clients.

Prefer per-client limits as the primary safety mechanism.

============================================================
PER-PRINCIPAL LIMIT
============================================================

Authenticated clients should normally be rate-limited by principal
or credential identity.

============================================================
PER-ENDPOINT LIMIT
============================================================

Different resources have different cost.

Examples:

    telemetry
    predictions
    analytics
    metadata

Do not assume all endpoints have equal cost.

============================================================
COST MODEL
============================================================

If weighted rate limiting is implemented:

    one request != necessarily one unit

For example:

    metadata read = 1
    telemetry query = 5
    large telemetry page = 10

ONLY implement a weighted model if the repository architecture
provides enough information to justify it.

Do not create arbitrary costs.

============================================================
DEFAULT MODEL
============================================================

Prefer a simple token-bucket style model if no existing mechanism
already exists.

The model should have:

    capacity
    refill rate
    current token state

Use an injected clock.

Do not use sleeps in tests.

============================================================
WHY TOKEN BUCKET
============================================================

A token bucket can support:

    short bursts
    sustained limits
    deterministic capacity

without requiring large request histories.

If the repository already uses another proven algorithm, reuse it
instead.

============================================================
BURST CONTROL
============================================================

Allow a bounded burst.

Do not allow:

    unlimited immediate requests

============================================================
REFILL
============================================================

Token refill must use a monotonic operational clock.

Do NOT use:

    race timestamp
    replay timestamp

for infrastructure rate limiting.

============================================================
CLOCK SEPARATION
============================================================

There are two distinct concepts:

    API rate-control time
    race/replay time

Keep them completely separate.

API rate limiting measures:

    real operational elapsed time

unless the architecture explicitly defines another mode.

============================================================
REPLAY
============================================================

Replay API traffic must still be protected.

Do NOT let replay simulation timestamps bypass real operational rate
limits.

============================================================
LIVE
============================================================

LIVE API traffic uses the same operational rate-control mechanism.

Do not rate-limit based on race lap/time.

============================================================
CLOCK INJECTION
============================================================

Implement a clock abstraction or reuse an existing injectable clock.

Tests must be deterministic.

Do not use real sleeping.

============================================================
NO SLEEP TESTS
============================================================

Never use:

    time.sleep()

to verify token refill/rate behaviour.

Advance a fake clock.

============================================================
429 RESPONSE
============================================================

REST rate-limit violations should use:

    HTTP 429 Too Many Requests

where appropriate.

Reuse Agent 17.1/17.3 error envelope.

============================================================
RETRY-AFTER
============================================================

When useful and calculable, expose:

    Retry-After

or equivalent metadata.

It must be:

    accurate
    bounded
    derived from actual limiter state

Do not invent retry values.

============================================================
RATE-LIMIT HEADERS
============================================================

If useful and supported by the chosen model, expose standard
metadata such as:

    remaining
    limit
    reset/retry information

Do not implement a proprietary header explosion.

Use a small consistent set.

============================================================
HEADER SEMANTICS
============================================================

Document whether values represent:

    current window
    token capacity
    refill state

Do not make ambiguous headers.

============================================================
WEBSOCKET RATE LIMIT
============================================================

WebSocket does not use HTTP 429 for every message after connection.

Define protocol-level rejection such as:

    RATE_LIMITED

with:

    reason_code
    retry information where meaningful

Use the Agent 17.4 public WS error model.

============================================================
WEBSOCKET LIMIT DIMENSIONS
============================================================

Protect at least, where justified:

    connection creation
    subscribe requests
    unsubscribe requests
    replay control messages
    per-client outbound consumption

Do NOT implement all dimensions unless useful.

============================================================
CONNECTION FLOOD
============================================================

Provide an architecture to limit excessive WebSocket connection
creation.

This may be:

    connection-attempt rate

rather than:

    maximum simultaneous connections

Do not confuse rate and concurrency.

============================================================
CONCURRENCY LIMIT
============================================================

If simultaneous WebSocket connections must be bounded, represent
that separately from request rate.

Potential:

    max_connections_per_principal
    max_connections_per_client

Only implement where actual system requirements justify it.

============================================================
SUBSCRIPTION FLOOD
============================================================

Limit:

    subscribe requests

and optionally:

    maximum active subscriptions per connection

Do not let a single client create unbounded subscriptions.

============================================================
CONTROL MESSAGE FLOOD
============================================================

Protect:

    subscribe
    unsubscribe
    replay control

from rapid client-driven message storms.

============================================================
DATA DELIVERY LIMIT
============================================================

Do NOT accidentally rate-limit internal telemetry generation.

The public API limiter controls external consumption.

Internal RaceVision runtime must continue independently.

============================================================
OUTBOUND VS INBOUND
============================================================

Distinguish:

    inbound control/request rate

from:

    outbound data volume.

Phase 11 may already provide outbound backpressure.

Reuse it.

Do NOT create a second outbound transport algorithm unnecessarily.

============================================================
TELEMETRY PROTECTION
============================================================

Telemetry is high-volume and expensive.

Public telemetry endpoints/subscriptions may require stronger
controls than metadata endpoints.

Use repository/query cost characteristics.

============================================================
LARGE QUERY PROTECTION
============================================================

Rate limiting alone is not sufficient.

Combine with:

    pagination
    maximum page size
    bounded time range

from Agent 17.3.

Do not allow:

    huge unbounded query × normal rate

to exhaust resources.

============================================================
QUERY COST
============================================================

If practical, rate-limit according to request cost.

However:

    do not invent a complex billing-style cost system.

============================================================
RATE LIMIT BY API VERSION
============================================================

API version may be included in the key/policy if different versions
have materially different costs.

Otherwise reuse the shared policy.

============================================================
RATE LIMIT BY ROUTE
============================================================

Route identity should be normalized.

Do not make dynamic path parameters create unlimited policy keys.

Example:

    /sessions/1
    /sessions/2
    /sessions/3

should generally map to:

    /sessions/{session_id}

not three unrelated limiter identities.

============================================================
HIGH-CARDINALITY KEY PROTECTION
============================================================

Never create an unbounded map where every arbitrary:

    query
    URL
    driver ID
    session ID

creates permanent limiter state.

Use:

    bounded eviction
    TTL
    maximum key count

============================================================
MEMORY BOUND
============================================================

Rate-limit state MUST be bounded.

This is mandatory.

Possible controls:

    max identities
    eviction TTL
    LRU
    expiration

Choose a deterministic bounded strategy.

============================================================
STALE LIMITER STATE
============================================================

Inactive client entries must eventually expire.

Do not retain identities forever.

============================================================
CLEANUP
============================================================

Implement bounded cleanup.

Do not run an uncontrolled background cleanup thread.

Prefer lazy cleanup or established infrastructure.

============================================================
DISTRIBUTED DEPLOYMENT
============================================================

Inspect whether RaceVision currently runs:

    single process
    multi-process
    multiple replicas

If single process:

    in-memory limiter may be sufficient for current architecture.

If multi-instance deployment is already supported:

    document that process-local rate limiting is not globally
    consistent unless a shared store exists.

Do NOT introduce Redis merely to claim distributed correctness.

============================================================
DISTRIBUTED LIMITATION
============================================================

If the deployment is multi-instance and no shared limiter exists:

    explicitly document:

        limits are per process/instance.

Do not claim global enforcement.

============================================================
ATOMICITY
============================================================

Rate-limit token consumption must be atomic within the chosen
concurrency model.

Do not allow concurrent requests to:

    both observe the same tokens
    and both exceed capacity.

============================================================
THREAD SAFETY
============================================================

Test concurrent requests.

Use:

    lock
    atomic primitive
    actor/event-loop confinement

according to repository architecture.

============================================================
ASYNC SAFETY
============================================================

If using asyncio:

    do not hold blocking locks across awaits.

============================================================
NO GLOBAL REQUEST STATE
============================================================

Do not store the current request globally.

============================================================
FAIL-CLOSED
============================================================

If rate-limit configuration is invalid:

    fail startup/configuration

or:

    deny protected traffic

according to repository conventions.

Do NOT silently disable rate limiting.

============================================================
FAIL-OPEN VS FAIL-CLOSED
============================================================

Operational policy must be explicit.

For security/resource protection, prefer:

    fail-closed

for invalid limiter configuration.

However, if an internal limiter component crashes unexpectedly,
avoid taking down canonical race runtime.

Isolate the public API failure boundary.

============================================================
LIMITER FAILURE ISOLATION
============================================================

Rate limiter failure must not crash:

    canonical runtime
    telemetry
    prediction
    analytics
    Director
    Unity
    OBS
    commentary
    TTS

Public API requests may fail closed.

============================================================
AUTHENTICATION INTERACTION
============================================================

Order:

    request
      ↓
    version
      ↓
    authentication
      ↓
    rate limit identity
      ↓
    authorization
      ↓
    application service

or the repository's equivalent.

The ordering must prevent anonymous abuse while still using principal
identity when available.

============================================================
PRE-AUTH RATE CONTROL
============================================================

Some protection may need to occur before authentication to prevent
credential brute force or connection flooding.

If implemented:

    use safe client/network identity

and then apply:

    principal-based limit

after authentication.

Do not create two unrelated rate-limit systems.

============================================================
AUTH FAILURE LIMITS
============================================================

If authentication failures themselves require rate limiting,
implement them as a policy dimension of the same rate-limit engine.

Do not build a separate credential-throttling engine.

============================================================
NO AUTHORIZATION LEAK
============================================================

Do not let rate-limit responses reveal sensitive resource existence.

Example:

    request for forbidden resource

must remain:

    authorization failure

rather than:

    rate-limit side channel

where the architecture requires it.

============================================================
RATE-LIMIT ERROR CONTENT
============================================================

Do not expose internal token counts or implementation details
unless they are part of the public contract.

============================================================
SECURITY
============================================================

Do not trust client-controlled headers for principal identity.

Do not allow clients to override:

    principal_id

through query parameters/body.

============================================================
CLIENT KEY SPOOFING
============================================================

A client must not be able to choose:

    X-Client-ID = someone-else

and receive their quota.

Client identifiers provided by clients may be advisory only.

============================================================
IP PRIVACY
============================================================

Do not unnecessarily persist raw client IP addresses.

If network identity is used:

    use transient/bounded representation.

Follow existing privacy/logging policy.

============================================================
NO IP BAN SYSTEM
============================================================

Do NOT implement:

    permanent IP bans
    blacklist databases

That is outside this agent.

============================================================
NO WAF
============================================================

Do not implement a Web Application Firewall.

============================================================
NO DDOS SERVICE
============================================================

Do not integrate external DDoS protection in Agent 17.6.

Document that edge/network-level DDoS protection belongs outside
the application.

============================================================
POLICY MODEL
============================================================

Create immutable policy configuration.

Potential structure:

    RateLimitPolicy

Fields may include:

    name
    capacity
    refill_rate
    refill_interval
    scope
    burst
    enabled
    retry_after
    max_keys

Use repository-native units.

============================================================
RATE LIMIT PROFILE
============================================================

Allow route/profile mapping such as:

    public-read
    telemetry-read
    analytics-read
    websocket-control

only where useful.

Do not create dozens of profiles.

============================================================
DEFAULT POLICY
============================================================

Choose conservative, documented defaults.

Do NOT invent production SLAs.

State clearly that defaults are:

    application safety defaults

not:

    capacity guarantees.

============================================================
PER-ROUTE CONFIGURATION
============================================================

Where route-specific limits exist:

    use explicit configuration.

Do not hide route limits inside decorators with unexplained constants.

============================================================
DISABLE POLICY
============================================================

If rate limiting can be disabled in development:

    make it explicit.

Production should not silently disable it.

============================================================
TEST ENVIRONMENT
============================================================

Tests may disable external/real client restrictions through explicit
test configuration.

Do not weaken production defaults merely to simplify tests.

============================================================
OBSERVABILITY HOOK
============================================================

Provide structured metadata for future Agent 17.11:

    decision
    policy
    scope
    client/principal identifier where safe
    endpoint
    API version
    retry-after
    reason

Do not build monitoring here.

============================================================
NO LOG FLOOD
============================================================

A rate-limited attack must not create a log flood.

Use existing logging levels.

Do not log every rejection at high severity by default.

============================================================
RATE LIMIT REASON CODES
============================================================

Use stable codes such as:

    RATE_LIMITED
    CONNECTION_RATE_LIMITED
    SUBSCRIPTION_RATE_LIMITED
    CONTROL_RATE_LIMITED
    QUOTA_EXCEEDED

Only create those actually used.

============================================================
DECISION MODEL
============================================================

Create immutable:

    RateLimitDecision

Potential fields:

    allowed
    policy_name
    scope
    key_hash/reference
    remaining
    retry_after_ms
    reason_code
    evaluated_at
    provenance

Do NOT expose raw secret/client credential material in the result.

============================================================
KEY PRIVACY
============================================================

If a rate-limit key is included in diagnostics:

    never expose raw API key/token.

Use:

    principal ID
    safe key ID
    hashed/transformed diagnostic representation

where needed.

============================================================
PROVENANCE
============================================================

Rate-limit decisions are operational control decisions.

They are not race-domain data.

Do not label them:

    canonical race state

============================================================
IMMUTABILITY
============================================================

Policy and decision models should be immutable.

============================================================
NO DATABASE
============================================================

Do NOT create database tables for rate-limit state unless existing
architecture explicitly requires distributed persistence.

Prefer bounded in-memory state for the current deployment model.

============================================================
NO REDIS/KAFKA BY DEFAULT
============================================================

Do not add:

    Redis
    Kafka
    RabbitMQ

merely to implement rate limiting.

============================================================
NO PUBLIC API CHANGES OTHER THAN NECESSARY ERRORS
============================================================

Do not add new public resources.

Do not add new REST endpoints.

Do not add new WebSocket channels.

============================================================
REST INTEGRATION
============================================================

Integrate the limiter centrally so routes do not each implement
rate logic independently.

Prefer middleware/dependency integration consistent with the HTTP
framework.

============================================================
WEBSOCKET INTEGRATION
============================================================

Integrate centrally with the public WebSocket boundary.

Rate-limit:

    connection
    control message
    subscription

as configured.

Do not duplicate Phase 11 transport backpressure.

============================================================
APPLICATION SERVICE SAFETY
============================================================

Rate limiting must happen BEFORE expensive application operations.

Do not:

    query database
    compute analytics
    build large response
    call external provider

and only then rate-limit.

============================================================
EARLY REJECTION
============================================================

Reject excessive requests as early as safely possible.

============================================================
RESPONSE COST
============================================================

Rate limiting must not itself create excessive CPU/memory work.

The limiter should be O(1) or near O(1) for normal operation.

============================================================
TOKEN BUCKET IMPLEMENTATION
============================================================

If implementing token bucket:

    tokens = min(capacity,
                 tokens + elapsed * refill_rate)

Allow when:

    tokens >= cost

Then:

    tokens -= cost

All numeric inputs must be:

    finite
    non-negative
    bounded

============================================================
FLOATING-POINT SAFETY
============================================================

Avoid pathological floating-point accumulation.

If repository conventions permit:

    use monotonic high-resolution time
    or integer micro/milliseconds

Document precision.

============================================================
NO NEGATIVE TOKENS
============================================================

Invariant:

    tokens >= 0

============================================================
NO OVER-CAPACITY TOKENS
============================================================

Invariant:

    tokens <= capacity

============================================================
REFILL TIME
============================================================

If no request occurs for a long time:

    bucket must refill only to capacity.

Do not accumulate infinite tokens.

============================================================
COST VALIDATION
============================================================

Cost must be:

    > 0
    <= maximum configured cost

A cost of:

    0

must not allow unlimited free requests.

============================================================
CONFIGURATION VALIDATION
============================================================

Reject:

    capacity <= 0
    refill_rate <= 0
    invalid interval
    negative burst
    invalid scope
    max_keys <= 0

============================================================
TIME OVERFLOW
============================================================

Avoid arithmetic that can overflow when:

    elapsed time is extremely large.

Bound/normalize elapsed values safely.

============================================================
CONCURRENT TOKEN CONSUMPTION
============================================================

Verify two simultaneous requests cannot both consume the same
available token state incorrectly.

============================================================
FAIRNESS
============================================================

Per-client rate limits should prevent one client from starving
others.

Global rate limits, if used, must be layered carefully.

============================================================
NO STARVATION
============================================================

High-priority/critical API operations should not be permanently
starved by normal traffic if the architecture explicitly has such
priority classes.

Do not invent complex priority scheduling.

============================================================
PRIORITY
============================================================

Do not create a general priority queue.

Rate limiting is not event prioritisation.

============================================================
WEBHOOK PREPARATION
============================================================

Agent 17.8 will use rate-limiting policy for future webhook
operations.

Provide a reusable policy interface.

Do NOT implement webhooks.

============================================================
STREAMING PREPARATION
============================================================

Agent 17.9 may use rate/quota controls.

Provide reusable policy boundary.

Do NOT implement streaming limits here beyond general architecture.

============================================================
SDK PREPARATION
============================================================

Agent 17.10 may consume:

    limit
    remaining
    retry-after

metadata.

Ensure error semantics are stable.

============================================================
MONITORING PREPARATION
============================================================

Agent 17.11 must be able to observe:

    allowed
    rejected
    scope
    policy
    endpoint
    API version
    reason

without accessing secrets.

============================================================
TESTING — MANDATORY
============================================================

Create focused rate-limit tests using the repository's existing test
structure.

At minimum test:

1. Package import.

2. Policy construction.

3. Policy immutability.

4. Policy validation.

5. Invalid capacity.

6. Invalid refill rate.

7. Invalid interval.

8. Invalid burst.

9. Invalid scope.

10. Limiter construction.

11. Decision model.

12. Decision immutability.

13. First request allowed.

14. Exact capacity boundary.

15. Capacity exceeded.

16. Token refill.

17. Exact refill boundary.

18. Long idle refill capped at capacity.

19. Burst allowed up to limit.

20. Sustained request enforcement.

21. Retry-after calculation.

22. Remaining calculation where exposed.

23. Zero/negative cost rejected.

24. Excessive cost rejected.

25. Non-finite cost rejected.

26. Non-finite elapsed time handled safely.

27. Negative elapsed time handled safely.

28. Clock injection.

29. No sleep.

30. Concurrent token consumption.

31. Per-principal isolation.

32. Per-client isolation.

33. Per-endpoint isolation.

34. Route normalization.

35. API-version policy behaviour.

36. Anonymous client handling.

37. Authenticated client handling.

38. Principal takes precedence over spoofable client ID.

39. Forwarded-IP spoofing does not bypass trusted-proxy policy.

40. Missing forwarded headers.

41. Trusted proxy handling where configured.

42. Untrusted proxy handling.

43. REST 429 response.

44. REST Retry-After where applicable.

45. REST error-envelope integration.

46. REST request is rejected before expensive service execution.

47. WebSocket rate-limit error.

48. WebSocket connection flood protection.

49. WebSocket subscribe flood protection.

50. WebSocket control-message flood protection.

51. WebSocket active subscription limit where implemented.

52. Duplicate subscription does not bypass limits.

53. Per-connection isolation.

54. Per-principal isolation across multiple connections.

55. Session A cannot consume Session B quota where session is not
    part of the configured scope.

56. Replay does not bypass operational rate control.

57. LIVE uses same operational rate semantics.

58. Race/replay timestamps do not control token refill.

59. Rate state expiration.

60. Maximum key count.

61. Bounded memory.

62. Lazy cleanup where implemented.

63. No unbounded limiter state.

64. Provider failure does not mutate limiter state incorrectly.

65. Limiter failure is isolated from canonical runtime.

66. Invalid configuration fails closed.

67. Production configuration does not silently disable limits.

68. Test configuration behaves explicitly.

69. Telemetry route receives stronger policy where configured.

70. Metadata route receives appropriate policy.

71. Different endpoints have isolated budgets where configured.

72. High-volume telemetry cannot bypass pagination limits.

73. Arbitrary query does not create unbounded limiter keys.

74. Arbitrary session/driver IDs do not create permanent keys.

75. Public API version included where policy requires.

76. Version v1 and v2 policies do not collide unexpectedly.

77. No secret appears in RateLimitDecision.

78. No API token appears in logs.

79. No Authorization header appears in logs.

80. No IP retention beyond configured bounded state.

81. No database writes.

82. No Redis/Kafka dependency.

83. No external network calls.

84. No AI/LLM.

85. No TTS.

86. No commentary generation.

87. No analytics mutation.

88. No prediction mutation.

89. No canonical mutation.

90. No Director control.

91. No OBS control.

92. No Unity control.

cost:

    1

cost:

    ALLOW

# 11. What Phase 18 should NOT do

I would **not** turn Phase 18 into another giant feature-development phase.

Its primary purpose should be:

```text
PHASES 1–17
     ↓
Find everything incomplete
     ↓
Fix engineering defects
     ↓
Complete missing production infrastructure
     ↓
Integrate real Unity
     ↓
Integrate real OBS
     ↓
Validate real providers
     ↓
Validate real telemetry
     ↓
Validate real race
     ↓
Production-ready RaceVision
```

# 12. The Phase 18 structure I recommend

I would expand the Phase 18 roadmap into these groups:

```text
18.1  Production Hardening Architecture + Master Defect Register
18.2  Full Regression Remediation
18.3  Repository Code Quality
18.4  Type Safety Hardening

18.5  Production API Deployment

```

But I would add a **parallel Production Content track**, because those assets should not be buried inside generic engineering agents:

## The most important conclusion

**RaceVision is no longer primarily missing backend architecture.**

The architecture through Phase 17 is substantial.

The remaining gap is now much more about:

**production hardening + real-world validation + 3D production assets + Unity scenes + OBS production scenes + live race integration.**

And the current repository confirms that the Unity/Blender directories exist as architectural boundaries, but they should not yet be treated as evidence that the actual F1 car/track/broadcast asset production is complete. fileciteturn79file0 fileciteturn80file0 fileciteturn81file0

The existing README also needs a major rewrite because it still says telemetry collectors, Unity, OBS, APIs and streaming are not implemented, which is no longer an accurate description of the later-phase repository. fileciteturn77file0

## The key point

We should **not** throw away the existing architecture and start again.

The project has reached the point where the work changes character:

**Phases 1–17 built the platform.  
Phase 18 should make the platform production-ready.  
A parallel asset/content programme should make the platform actually look like an F1 broadcast.**

The next logical artifact is therefore a **master Phase 18 + Production Content roadmap**, where every item above gets a unique owner agent, dependency, acceptance criteria, and definition of done.

## User

Please give me a full list of Agents and Components for Phase 18 for Production Content

## Assistant

Yes. I recommend making **Phase 18 Production Content** a dedicated production-content programme alongside the engineering-hardening agents, rather than mixing 3D/graphics work into the backend hardening agents.

The purpose of this phase is to take RaceVision from:

**“the software architecture can render a digital twin”**

to:

**“we actually have the cars, circuits, scenes, cameras, graphics, audio, effects, and broadcast package required to produce a convincing live F1-style digital broadcast.”**
